question: Should OpenClaw permanently support operator-selected core readiness criteria and the new plugin `registerReadinessCriterion` API, rather than keeping deployment-specific checks outside the core contract?
rationale: This is an optional feature with new configuration and plugin API surface that can intentionally change host admission behavior; implementation quality alone cannot choose that product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core readiness contract
options.body: Accept the direction, require the framework-first landing order, upgrade proof, and a maintained plugin API contract.

options.title: Keep readiness deployment-owned
options.body: Decline the new core and SDK surfaces and retain existing host-specific readiness checks outside OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded core readiness contract
recommendation.body: Accept the direction, require the framework-first landing order, upgrade proof, and a maintained plugin API contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the related readiness stack and can clarify the intended contract, while a repository owner must make the final product decision.
